title: Gift Wrap Roll

drivers.name: Price increase (3.4%)
drivers.evidence: Past price changes show no consistent demand impact; noise-adjusted promotion lifts are x1.0; no evidence of price sensitivity in history

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 3.1. No events or promotions are planned for the target week. The price increase to $5.72 (+3.4%) is notable, but past promotions at similar or deeper discounts show weak, noise-adjusted lift (x1.0). The target week is 8 weeks after the last data, in the post-Thanksgiving holiday window, but no seasonal ramp is visible in the baseline. The historical trend is up 34% over 13 weeks, but the baseline already reflects this. No evidence of pantry-loading effects. The classical model suggests no lift, and the noise-adjusted promotion history supports x1.0. Price increase may slightly reduce demand, but no past price hike has shown a measurable effect. The median multiplier remains 1.0. Spreads unchanged.

PRODUCT: Gift Wrap Roll | category Seasonal | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-06 (8 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 5.72 (+3.4% vs regular price 5.53)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 3.1 | 5%-95%: 0.0 - 11.0 | 10%-90%: 0.0 - 9.4

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-95% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
